title: Throughput contract guardrails and autoscale interlock playbook
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Define a standardized, legally defensible throughput SLA for Dedicated customers plus a paired error-budget and credit computation method; specify autoscaler interlock policies and fleet-control fallback behavior; produce contract wording and an internal ops playbook for incident handling and remediation.
acceptance_criteria: Drafted SLA clause with measurable throughput metric (quantile, window) and clear measurement source
Error budget calculation documented and verified against production telemetry with sample computations
Credit formula and notice windows specified in plain language and legal-ready wording
Autoscale interlock policy defined (triggers, limits, cooldowns) and mapped to failover behavior
Ops playbook created with step-by-step remediation, notification templates, and runbook links
Legal sign-off on contract language and Sales enablement doc completed
comments: 2026-03-05 Sofia Patel: Created ticket after customer advisory meeting where several enterprise customers requested deterministic throughput guarantees and a clear remediation path. Initial ask: per-customer tokens/minute guarantee with 99th percentile measurement. Need to reconcile legal appetite for quantile vs. floor guarantees.

2026-03-06 Marcus Nguyen: Spike results from ENG-88212 show high variance in short windows; recommendation is to use a 95th-percentile over a 24-hour sliding window for token throughput to avoid spurious failures from microbursts. Drafted sample computation in Confluence.

2026-03-07 Legal (Priya Rao): Prefer language that ties SLA to quantifiable telemetry source and makes credits proportional to measurable shortfall. Legal requests clear notice windows and opportunity to remediate before credits apply (default 3 business days).

2026-03-08 Reliability (Jae Park): Proposed error budget expressed as percentage of committed throughput over a billing period, with two-stage crediting: immediate shortfall credit (pro rata for the affected day) and cumulative monthly reconciliation if error budget exceeded. Need to determine caps to avoid unbounded liability.

2026-03-09 Marcus Nguyen: Drafted autoscale interlock: when observed throughput drops below 85% of committed target for >10 minutes, autoscaler may prioritize customer pool with a bounded burst from shared capacity (burst cap = 20% of committed baseline) for up to 30 minutes. If sustained >1 hour, trigger operational incident and notify customer. Documented fallback to best-effort public pool when dedicated pool exhausted.

2026-03-10 Sofia Patel: Trade-off note — using a 24h 95th quantile smooths noise but may hide systemic regressions that occur only during peak hours. Proposal: pair the 24h quantile SLA with a short-window alert (5m P50) for ops-only detection without affecting credit calculations.

2026-03-11 Engineering (Jae Park): Implemented telemetry tag 'committed_customer_id' and a new aggregated metric 'dedicated_throughput_q95_24h' in telemetry pipeline. ENG-90501 PR drafted to expose measurement in the SLO API. Need QA on aggregation correctness across AZ failovers.

2026-03-12 Sales feedback (Emma Lewis): Sales wants a simple customer-facing summary: Guaranteed throughput = 95th percentile of per-minute tokens measured over 24h. Credits = (committed - delivered)/committed * monthly fee * credit_factor. Request template language for quoting and SOWs.

2026-03-13 Legal sign-off (Priya Rao): Approved plain-language SLA appendix and credit formula with cap at 20% of monthly committed fee per incident and cumulative cap at 50% for a billing period. Requires inclusion of force-majeure and maintenance windows. Added required notice period of 3 business days before credits apply and immediate notification requirement from Redwood.

2026-03-14 Marcus Nguyen: Preparing ops playbook draft and incident notification templates. Next: finalize autoscale interlock knobs with ENG and run a chaostest simulating AZ starvation (2026-03-20). Also scheduling a 30-min cross-functional review with Sales and Legal on 2026-03-16.
resolution_notes: In-progress: core SLA language approved by Legal. Engineering needs to finish metric exposure (ENG-90501) and add alerting for short-window regressions. Ops playbook draft live in Confluence; runbook tests scheduled. Sales templates being prepared for tomorrow's enablement session.
